chunks: And he wrote to him regarding

A man said to two men: "Bear witness that the entire house which he owns in such-and-such a place, with all its boundaries, belongs to so-and-so son of so-and-so, along with all that he has in the house of furnishings." But the witnesses did not know what the furnishings were, which thing they were.
So he signed, عليه السلام: "It is valid if the purchase encompasses all of that, if Allah wills."

key_terms.الدَّارِ: The house or property being transferred.
key_terms.الشِّرَاءُ: The purchase; the contractual acquisition covering the property and contents.
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: The witnesses or evidentiary testimony referred to in the transaction.
key_terms.الْمَتَاعِ: The belongings or furnishings contained within the house.
key_terms.اِشْهَدَا: Bear witness; a directive to formalize the matter through testimony.
key_terms.بِحُدُودِهَا: With its boundaries; indicating the defined limits of the property.
key_terms.يَصْلُحُ: It is valid or sound in legal effect.

ai.seo_question: Is the sale of a house and all its contents valid if the witnesses do not know each item individually?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal validity of a transaction involving a house and all its contents when the witnesses do not specifically know the individual items of property. The Imam عليه السلام rules that it is valid so long as the purchase comprehensively includes all of it. The narration is significant for jurisprudence on sales, testimony, and contractual scope.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3885 - He wrote to Imam (as) regarding a man who said to two witnesses,
"Bear witness that the entire house which he owns in such-and-such a location, with all its boundaries, belongs to so-and-so, along with all the belongings he has in the house."
However, the witnesses did not know what the belongings were.
Imam (as) responded: "It is valid if the purchase encompasses all of that, if Allah (swt) wills."
